title: A Machine Learning Model for the Accurate Prediction of 1-Year Survival in TAVI Patients: A Retrospective Observational Cohort Study
summary: An earlier PMU Science Get Together abstract reported ML prediction of one-year mortality in the same 629-patient TAVI cohort using the same model family and reject option (NPV 98%, PPV 89% after abstaining on 145/447); the later journal article reports revised metrics (NPV 96%, PPV 92%). The retrospective, single-center result remains limited by selective abstention. Machine-learning models predicted one-year survival after TAVI, with 10-fold cross-validation and a separate test sample; a random-forest reject-option subgroup yielded 96% accuracy. This retrospective cohort result is limited by selective abstention and single-center data.
ai_technology: Five ML approaches including RF/SVM trained in learning samples using 10-fold CV, then evaluated in held-out test data. 629 transfemoral TAVI patients; 565 had one-year outcome. With reject option, model predicts for a subset (~81% of original cohort) with reported accuracy 96%, NPV 96%, PPV 92%.
